points.quote: Neither basis is factoring or discrete log
points.problem: 'basis' is used for the first time here; the lattice passage only speaks of 'directions', and never says that the long skewed set is the public key. A newcomer cannot tell which two bases are meant.
points.hint: Say 'set of directions' throughout (or name 'basis' once) and state that the skewed set is public, the short set private.

points.quote: reveal the secrets the message's own hash picks out
points.problem: How a hash 'picks out' secrets is unexplained, and so is why revealing some secrets does not give away the key or why each key is 'one-use'. The hash-based signature is a slogan at this point.
points.hint: One concrete clause: e.g. each bit of the message hash decides which of two secrets is revealed; revealed secrets are spent, hence one-use.

points.quote: So a 256-bit hash holds out against collisions only to about 2^128 work
points.problem: The caption jumps from 'pairs grow as the square' (365 days, 253 pairs) to 2^128 without saying that a match is expected once the pair count nears the number of possible hashes, so the work is about the square root of 2^256. The reader must infer the step.
points.hint: Add the link: about N pairs are needed to hit N possible values, so roughly the square root of N inputs suffice.

points.quote: keeps the key from leaking through timing
points.problem: Why running time could leak a secret key is never explained anywhere earlier in the book, so 'constant-time' reads as jargon.
points.hint: A short clause: work that takes longer for some key bits lets an observer measure those bits.

points.quote: HKDF stretches it, mixed with a hash of the conversation
points.problem: HKDF and 'transcript' are used in the figure and caption but never explained in the prose or earlier; only the strip says what goes into the transcript. The reader sees labelled boxes without knowing what HKDF does.
points.hint: Gloss HKDF once as 'a function that turns one shared secret into several separate keys' and 'transcript' as the handshake messages so far.

points.quote: undo modular powers (the discrete logarithm of Section 04)
points.problem: 'discrete logarithm' is named before it is taught (Section 04), and Fig 14.2 also relies on it as a row title; the primer's own text gives only a forward pointer.
points.hint: Name it in plain words here ('finding the exponent from a modular power') and keep the Section 04 pointer.
